// purpose: @debuggen/panel-renderer - the compiler project for the monorepo typecheck gate. `pnpm typecheck` (= `pnpm demo:generate && tsc -b`) builds the root solution file, whose `references` list this project after packages/shared, packages/telemetry, packages/code-analysis, packages/instrumentation and packages/panel-schema: the renderer sits at the top of the library half of the acyclic package graph (AAP 0.2.2) and depends on three workspaces - shared, telemetry and panel-schema - so `references` below has exactly those three entries, foundational-first, and `tsc -b` builds them before this project.
// consumers: Three consumers read this one file and all three must stay satisfied: (1) the solution build `tsc -b`, which requires `composite` (see below); (2) the sibling `tsup.config.ts`, which points at it with `tsconfig: "./tsconfig.json"` for the bundle and the declaration pass, so the shipped artefacts and the gate type-check under one configuration; (3) typescript-eslint's project service, which resolves the type information behind the type-aware rules and `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` for `src/**/*.tsx` - which is why the colocated tests are inside `include`.
// package: What this package is: the in-repo design system (AAP 0.6) - one token source (src/tokens/tokens.ts, from which scripts/build-tokens.mjs generates src/tokens/tokens.css), the UI primitives, the layout primitives, the thirteen visualization components of the node catalog and the `PanelHost` that renders only validated panel specifications. It is browser-only React code: it renders inside the Chrome DevTools panel and the VS Code webview, and it reaches data exclusively through the `DataProvider`/`PanelActions` interfaces it declares, never through a socket or `fetch` of its own.
// ambient-css: NOT declared anywhere in this package: an ambient `*.css` module. No TypeScript file here imports a stylesheet - tsup.config.ts concatenates src/tokens/tokens.css, src/styles/base.css and src/styles/components.css into dist/styles.css, which the two consumers import as "@debuggen/panel-renderer/styles.css". A need for a `declare module "*.css"` means a source file grew a CSS import that must be removed instead, because it would also break `"sideEffects": ["**/*.css"]` and consumer tree-shaking.
// inherited: Everything not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, the no-unused/no-implicit diagnostics, `target` ES2023 and the declaration-emit settings (`declaration`, `declarationMap`, `sourceMap`, `emitDeclarationOnly`, `incremental`). `noEmit` must never be added: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects a referenced project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails.
// format: Strict JSON, like tsconfig.base.json, the root tsconfig.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` can read it, so no consumer has to know which one to reach for. tsc, ESLint, Vitest, tsup and Prettier would all accept comments in a tsconfig file, but the rationale is recorded in the `"// …"` string keys of this object instead so that every reader gets it. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because the root solution file references this project and a non-composite reference fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate at this project. The declaration pass of tsup is the one consumer that may need the opposite value; when it does, it overrides `composite` inside tsup.config.ts (`dts: { compilerOptions: { composite: false } }`) - never by removing it from here, which would break `pnpm typecheck` repository-wide.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: Per-workspace (the base deliberately leaves it unset), so the declaration tree under .tsbuild/ mirrors src/ exactly: src/index.ts -> .tsbuild/index.d.ts and src/components/Timeline.tsx -> .tsbuild/components/Timeline.d.ts, matching the path the package.json `exports` map advertises under dist/. It also pins the program's boundary: nothing outside src/ may be an input, which is what keeps scripts/build-tokens.mjs out of the program (`allowJs` stays false, and that script is linted, never compiled).
// compilerOptions.lib: Widened from the base's ES2023-only set, which exists so that a Node-only package cannot reference `window` and still compile. This project is the opposite case: every module renders in a page. The components legitimately use `document`, `ResizeObserver`, `Element.getBoundingClientRect`, `KeyboardEvent`/`PointerEvent`, the SVG interfaces behind the timeline, flame, waterfall and dependency-graph views (`SVGSVGElement`, `SVGGElement`), and `window.matchMedia` for resolving the high-contrast and colour-scheme preference in src/tokens/theme.ts. DOM.Iterable is what makes iteration over `NodeList`, `DOMTokenList` and `SVGElement` children type-check. ES2023 is restated alongside the browser libs because `lib` REPLACES the inherited array rather than merging with it - omitting ES2023 here would silently drop `Array.prototype.findLast`, `toSorted` and the rest, all of which the sorting and grouping helpers in src/utils/** rely on. No "DOM.AsyncIterable" and no "WebWorker": nothing in this package streams from a `ReadableStream` or runs off the main thread.
// compilerOptions.types: The base sets no `types` so that one workspace's ambient globals cannot bleed into another. This project needs exactly one: @types/node 24.13.6 (a root devDependency, resolved through the workspace-root node_modules/@types). It exists for ONE colocated test - src/tokens/tokens.test.ts - which reads the generated src/tokens/tokens.css from disk with `node:fs` to make the byte-wise drift assertion AAP 0.6.1 requires (the committed CSS must match what src/tokens/tokens.ts generates). The Vitest project for this package runs under happy-dom, where `node:*` builtins keep working. THE BOUNDARY THIS DOES NOT MOVE: no non-test module under src/** may import a `node:*` builtin or touch `process`/`Buffer`/`require`. The compiler cannot express "ambient in tests only", so the guarantee is mechanical instead - tsup.config.ts sets `platform: "browser"`, which fails the build if a Node builtin appears anywhere in the src/index.ts import graph, and the colocated `*.test.ts(x)` files are not build inputs. Anything that needs a filesystem, a socket or an environment variable belongs in the host application (apps/chrome-extension, apps/vscode-extension) or in apps/local-service. Not listed: "react" / "react-dom". They are not ambient global type packages. JSX types arrive through the automatic runtime's `react/jsx-runtime` module import, and component code writes `import type { ReactNode } from "react"`; naming them here would instead make React's globals ambient package-wide. Not listed: "vitest/globals". The Vitest project for this package sets `globals: true` only so @testing-library/react can register its automatic `cleanup` on the global `afterEach`; the suites themselves still import `{ describe, it, expect }` from "vitest" explicitly, exactly as every sibling package does.
// compilerOptions.module: NOT overridden: "module" / "moduleResolution". The base's "ESNext" + "bundler" is the correct flavour for this package and AAP 0.3.4 assigns it: bundler resolution for web and extension code, NodeNext only for the Node-targeted packages. Nothing here is ever loaded by Node - the two consumers bundle dist/index.js with Vite - so the stricter Node flavour would buy nothing and cost the whole source tree an extension convention. CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY SOURCE FILE IN src/**, and the single most likely avoidable break in this workspace: relative specifiers are EXTENSIONLESS - `import { Button } from "./Button";`, `import { resolveTheme } from "../tokens/theme";`, `export * from "./host/PanelHost";` - which is the exact OPPOSITE of the ".js"-suffixed convention that packages/shared, packages/telemetry and packages/panel-schema must use because they override this setting to NodeNext. Copying an import line from one of those packages into this one is a compile error (TS2307: the file "./Button.js" does not exist), and the mistake reads as correct. Package specifiers are written without an extension in both flavours - "react", "clsx", "@debuggen/panel-schema" - and resolve through the pnpm workspace symlink and each package's `exports` map.
// compilerOptions.jsx: NOT overridden. The base already sets "react-jsx" (React 19.3.0 automatic runtime), so no .tsx file in this package needs an `import React`.
// compilerOptions.outDir: NOT overridden: "outDir" / "declarationDir" / "tsBuildInfoFile". The base anchors all three per project with `${configDir}`, which resolves to the directory of THIS file and not to the base's own directory, so declarations and the incremental stamp land in packages/panel-renderer/.tsbuild - ignored by .gitignore and .prettierignore. tsc must never write into packages/panel-renderer/dist: that directory belongs to tsup and holds dist/index.js, dist/index.d.ts and the assembled dist/styles.css that the `exports` map points at.
// compilerOptions.paths: NOT set: "paths" / "baseUrl". The three workspace dependencies resolve through their `exports` maps plus the project references below, as the root tsconfig.json `"// no-aliases"` note records. An alias to a sibling's src/** would hide a broken `exports` map, let this package import internals past a declared entry point, and let the acyclic layering be violated without anything failing.
// compilerOptions.noEmit: NOT set, and no strictness flag is relaxed on top of the base.
// include: src/** only, and both extensions: the components, primitives, layout, PanelHost and NodeRenderer are .tsx, while the host interfaces, registry and hooks, the tokens and the utils are .ts. The colocated `*.test.ts(x)` suites are deliberately part of the program, because `tsc -b` is the typecheck gate and an untypechecked test is how contract drift escapes; `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` apply to them exactly as to the sources. The same globs give typescript-eslint's project service a program covering every linted file here. Not included, on purpose: the scripts/ Node tooling (linted, never compiled - `allowJs` stays false) and the *.css files, which are data for tsup and tokens.test.ts, not program inputs.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list rather than merging with it, so the output directories are named again here; resolved relative to this directory, meaning packages/panel-renderer/{dist,.tsbuild,node_modules}. `include` already restricts the input set to src/**, which leaves dist/ (tsup output) and .tsbuild/ (declaration output) outside the program; these entries document that intent and keep it true if `include` is ever widened. Note what `exclude` does NOT do: it filters the `include` globs only, so a file reached by an import still joins the program - `rootDir` above is what rejects one from outside src/ (TS6059).
// references: Exactly this package's workspace `dependencies`. They make `tsc -b` build those projects first and substitute their .tsbuild declarations for the src/ entries the `exports` maps name (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3). Never add ../protocol or an app: data arrives only through this package's `DataProvider`/`PanelActions`, eslint.config.js `no-restricted-imports` forbids either import, and both extension apps consume this package, so referencing one is a cycle `tsc -b` rejects.
